criteria.text: Home (out-of-center) sleep testing is not covered for diagnosing obstructive sleep apnea when the patient has a significant comorbid medical condition or sleep disorder that may make the test inaccurate, such as moderate to severe lung disease, neuromuscular disease or congestive heart failure.

criteria.policy_title: CT and MRI of the head and neck
criteria.text: A scan with contrast needs a documented reason: assessing perfusion (such as a stroke), characterizing a specific lesion, detecting a blood-brain barrier defect (such as infarct, tumor, infection or vasculitis) or new blood vessels in a tumor, new-onset seizures (particularly with a focal component), or staging a known lung cancer, breast cancer or lymphoma likely to spread early to the brain. After head trauma, contrast generally adds nothing unless symptoms suggest a possible bleed inside the skull. More than one contrast scan per episode of illness is not covered except for stroke, TIA, non-traumatic bleeding, a post-operative scan for residual tumor or a complication, or a known brain tumor or metastases with a change in mental status or other sign of central nervous system change.
criteria.source: LCD L37373 v41 cov-015, cov-023 to cov-035.

criteria.text: Active wound care (debridement) is covered to remove dead tissue and promote healing, performed with direct one-on-one patient contact, following accepted standards of wound treatment.

Care must be part of a plan that addresses complicating factors (pressure off-loading, infection, poor circulation, metabolic or nutritional problems), aiming at wound closure or, when healing is not possible, preventing the wound from getting worse.

How often debridement is done depends on the wound. When the goal of care is healing, a given type of wound care is not continued if the record does not show improvement leading to healing, and when the expected healing is not documented after 30 days the plan of care should be revised. When the goal of care is not healing, the patient is managed under palliative care standards.

Routine foot care is covered for nerve damage in the feet (without blood-vessel impairment) severe enough that care by a non-professional would put the patient at risk. The record must document loss of protective sensation: no feeling at 2 or more of 5 sites on either foot with the 5.07 Semmes-Weinstein monofilament.
It is covered for patients on blood thinners when the record documents the significant risk of non-professional foot care.

Foot care that would otherwise be routine is covered when a systemic condition, such as diabetes, arteriosclerosis obliterans, Buerger's disease, chronic thrombophlebitis or a peripheral neuropathy involving the feet, causes severe circulatory problems or areas of reduced sensation in the legs or feet, so that care by a non-professional would be hazardous. A diagnosis alone does not show the severity: the record must show it, for example by a non-traumatic amputation of the foot or part of it; two Class B findings (absent posterior tibial pulse, absent dorsalis pedis pulse, or advanced trophic changes, three of which are needed); or one Class B and two Class C findings (claudication, temperature changes such as cold feet, edema, paresthesias, burning). For diabetes, chronic thrombophlebitis and the neuropathies marked in the manual, the patient must be under the active care of a doctor of medicine or osteopathy who documents the condition.

criteria.text: Patients identified as high risk for colon cancer are eligible for continued screening every 24 months.

Colonoscopy to investigate symptoms or findings is covered for: an imaging abnormality likely to be significant; unexplained bleeding (blood in the stool not thought to be from a rectal or perianal source, black tarry stool of unknown origin, or a positive stool blood test); unexplained iron-deficiency anemia; significant unexplained diarrhea with other findings such as weight loss; examining the whole colon for synchronous cancer or polyps in a patient with a treatable cancer or polyp; chronic inflammatory bowel disease when a more precise diagnosis or the extent of activity will change immediate management; locating during surgery a lesion that cannot be found by touch or sight; acute colonic ischemia; Streptococcus bovis endocarditis; unexplained new-onset constipation that does not respond to medical treatment; an anorectal adenomatous polyp; or infectious colitis.
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-007, cov-009 to cov-012, cov-014, cov-022 to cov-026, cov-032, cov-033, doc-001.

criteria.text: Surveillance is covered for a history of colorectal cancer or polyps, follow-up one year after colorectal cancer surgery, follow-up after removal of a large sessile adenoma (more than 2 cm in its greatest dimension), and inflammatory bowel disease surveillance (pancolitis for more than 7 years, or left-sided colitis for more than 15 years; not for disease limited to the rectosigmoid).
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-013, cov-015, cov-017, cov-019 to cov-021.

criteria.text: Colonoscopy is generally not covered, unless the record documents why it is needed, for: chronic, stable irritable bowel syndrome or chronic abdominal pain (in unusual cases it may be done to rule out organic disease, especially when symptoms do not respond to therapy); acute diarrhea; hemorrhoids; routine follow-up of inflammatory bowel disease (cancer surveillance in Crohn's disease or chronic ulcerative colitis excepted); routine examination before elective abdominal surgery for a non-colonic disease; upper GI bleeding or black tarry stool with a demonstrated upper GI source; or bright red rectal bleeding with a convincing anorectal source on sigmoidoscopy and no other symptoms suggesting a source higher up. It is also generally not covered for fulminant colitis, possible perforation, acute severe diverticulitis, or diverticulosis as the reason for the test (it may still be reported when it is the final diagnosis).

criteria.text: Active wound care (debridement) is covered to remove dead tissue and promote healing, performed with direct one-on-one patient contact, following accepted standards of wound treatment.

Care must be part of a plan that addresses complicating factors (pressure off-loading, infection, poor circulation, metabolic or nutritional problems), aiming at wound closure or, when healing is not possible, preventing the wound from getting worse.

How often debridement is done depends on the wound. When the goal of care is healing, a given type of wound care is not continued if the record does not show improvement leading to healing, and when the expected healing is not documented after 30 days the plan of care should be revised. When the goal of care is not healing, the patient is managed under palliative care standards.

criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-007, cov-009 to cov-012, cov-014, cov-022 to cov-026, cov-032, cov-033, doc-001.

criteria.text: Surveillance is covered for a history of colorectal cancer or polyps, follow-up one year after colorectal cancer surgery, follow-up after removal of a large sessile adenoma (more than 2 cm in its greatest dimension), and inflammatory bowel disease surveillance (pancolitis for more than 7 years, or left-sided colitis for more than 15 years; not for disease limited to the rectosigmoid).
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-013, cov-015, cov-017, cov-019 to cov-021.

criteria.text: Colonoscopy is generally not covered, unless the record documents why it is needed, for: chronic, stable irritable bowel syndrome or chronic abdominal pain (in unusual cases it may be done to rule out organic disease, especially when symptoms do not respond to therapy); acute diarrhea; hemorrhoids; routine follow-up of inflammatory bowel disease (cancer surveillance in Crohn's disease or chronic ulcerative colitis excepted); routine examination before elective abdominal surgery for a non-colonic disease; upper GI bleeding or black tarry stool with a demonstrated upper GI source; or bright red rectal bleeding with a convincing anorectal source on sigmoidoscopy and no other symptoms suggesting a source higher up. It is also generally not covered for fulminant colitis, possible perforation, acute severe diverticulitis, or diverticulosis as the reason for the test (it may still be reported when it is the final diagnosis).

criteria.text: Colonoscopy is also covered to treat: bleeding from lesions such as vascular anomalies, ulceration or tumors; a foreign body (removal); colonic polyps (excision); pseudo-obstruction of the colon (Ogilvie's syndrome, decompression); sigmoid volvulus or stricture; or narrowing or bleeding tumors, as palliative treatment (for example laser, electrocoagulation or stenting).
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-006, cov-027 to cov-031, cov-034.

criteria.text: Patients identified as high risk for colon cancer are eligible for continued screening every 24 months.

Colonoscopy to investigate symptoms or findings is covered for: an imaging abnormality likely to be significant; unexplained bleeding (blood in the stool not thought to be from a rectal or perianal source, black tarry stool of unknown origin, or a positive stool blood test); unexplained iron-deficiency anemia; significant unexplained diarrhea with other findings such as weight loss; examining the whole colon for synchronous cancer or polyps in a patient with a treatable cancer or polyp; chronic inflammatory bowel disease when a more precise diagnosis or the extent of activity will change immediate management; locating during surgery a lesion that cannot be found by touch or sight; acute colonic ischemia; Streptococcus bovis endocarditis; unexplained new-onset constipation that does not respond to medical treatment; an anorectal adenomatous polyp; or infectious colitis.
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-007, cov-009 to cov-012, cov-014, cov-022 to cov-026, cov-032, cov-033, doc-001.

criteria.text: Surveillance is covered for a history of colorectal cancer or polyps, follow-up one year after colorectal cancer surgery, follow-up after removal of a large sessile adenoma (more than 2 cm in its greatest dimension), and inflammatory bowel disease surveillance (pancolitis for more than 7 years, or left-sided colitis for more than 15 years; not for disease limited to the rectosigmoid).
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-013, cov-015, cov-017, cov-019 to cov-021.

criteria.text: Colonoscopy is generally not covered, unless the record documents why it is needed, for: chronic, stable irritable bowel syndrome or chronic abdominal pain (in unusual cases it may be done to rule out organic disease, especially when symptoms do not respond to therapy); acute diarrhea; hemorrhoids; routine follow-up of inflammatory bowel disease (cancer surveillance in Crohn's disease or chronic ulcerative colitis excepted); routine examination before elective abdominal surgery for a non-colonic disease; upper GI bleeding or black tarry stool with a demonstrated upper GI source; or bright red rectal bleeding with a convincing anorectal source on sigmoidoscopy and no other symptoms suggesting a source higher up. It is also generally not covered for fulminant colitis, possible perforation, acute severe diverticulitis, or diverticulosis as the reason for the test (it may still be reported when it is the final diagnosis).
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-036 to cov-039, cov-041 to cov-049.

criteria.text: Colonoscopy is also covered to treat: bleeding from lesions such as vascular anomalies, ulceration or tumors; a foreign body (removal); colonic polyps (excision); pseudo-obstruction of the colon (Ogilvie's syndrome, decompression); sigmoid volvulus or stricture; or narrowing or bleeding tumors, as palliative treatment (for example laser, electrocoagulation or stenting).
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-006, cov-027 to cov-031, cov-034.

criteria.text: Active wound care (debridement) is covered to remove dead tissue and promote healing, performed with direct one-on-one patient contact, following accepted standards of wound treatment.

How often debridement is done depends on the wound. When the goal of care is healing, a given type of wound care is not continued if the record does not show improvement leading to healing, and when the expected healing is not documented after 30 days the plan of care should be revised. When the goal of care is not healing, the patient is managed under palliative care standards.

Foot care that would otherwise be routine is covered when a systemic condition, such as diabetes, arteriosclerosis obliterans, Buerger's disease, chronic thrombophlebitis or a peripheral neuropathy involving the feet, causes severe circulatory problems or areas of reduced sensation in the legs or feet, so that care by a non-professional would be hazardous. criteria.text: Routine foot care is covered for nerve damage in the feet (without blood-vessel impairment) severe enough that care by a non-professional would put the patient at risk. The record must document loss of protective sensation: no feeling at 2 or more of 5 sites on either foot with the 5.07 Semmes-Weinstein monofilament.
It is covered for patients on blood thinners when the record documents the significant risk of non-professional foot care.

Foot care that would otherwise be routine is covered when a systemic condition, such as diabetes, arteriosclerosis obliterans, Buerger's disease, chronic thrombophlebitis or a peripheral neuropathy involving the feet, causes severe circulatory problems or areas of reduced sensation in the legs or feet, so that care by a non-professional would be hazardous. A diagnosis alone does not show the severity: the record must show it, for example by a non-traumatic amputation of the foot or part of it; two Class B findings (absent posterior tibial pulse, absent dorsalis pedis pulse, or advanced trophic changes, three of which are needed); or one Class B and two Class C findings (claudication, temperature changes such as cold feet, edema, paresthesias, burning). For diabetes, chronic thrombophlebitis and the neuropathies marked in the manual, the patient must be under the active care of a doctor of medicine or osteopathy who documents the condition.

criteria.text: Patients identified as high risk for colon cancer are eligible for continued screening every 24 months.

Colonoscopy to investigate symptoms or findings is covered for: an imaging abnormality likely to be significant; unexplained bleeding (blood in the stool not thought to be from a rectal or perianal source, black tarry stool of unknown origin, or a positive stool blood test); unexplained iron-deficiency anemia; significant unexplained diarrhea with other findings such as weight loss; examining the whole colon for synchronous cancer or polyps in a patient with a treatable cancer or polyp; chronic inflammatory bowel disease when a more precise diagnosis or the extent of activity will change immediate management; locating during surgery a lesion that cannot be found by touch or sight; acute colonic ischemia; Streptococcus bovis endocarditis; unexplained new-onset constipation that does not respond to medical treatment; an anorectal adenomatous polyp; or infectious colitis.
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-007, cov-009 to cov-012, cov-014, cov-022 to cov-026, cov-032, cov-033, doc-001.

criteria.text: Surveillance is covered for a history of colorectal cancer or polyps, follow-up one year after colorectal cancer surgery, follow-up after removal of a large sessile adenoma (more than 2 cm in its greatest dimension), and inflammatory bowel disease surveillance (pancolitis for more than 7 years, or left-sided colitis for more than 15 years; not for disease limited to the rectosigmoid).
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-013, cov-015, cov-017, cov-019 to cov-021.

criteria.text: Colonoscopy is generally not covered, unless the record documents why it is needed, for: chronic, stable irritable bowel syndrome or chronic abdominal pain (in unusual cases it may be done to rule out organic disease, especially when symptoms do not respond to therapy); acute diarrhea; hemorrhoids; routine follow-up of inflammatory bowel disease (cancer surveillance in Crohn's disease or chronic ulcerative colitis excepted); routine examination before elective abdominal surgery for a non-colonic disease; upper GI bleeding or black tarry stool with a demonstrated upper GI source; or bright red rectal bleeding with a convincing anorectal source on sigmoidoscopy and no other symptoms suggesting a source higher up. It is also generally not covered for fulminant colitis, possible perforation, acute severe diverticulitis, or diverticulosis as the reason for the test (it may still be reported when it is the final diagnosis).
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-036 to cov-039, cov-041 to cov-049.

criteria.text: Colonoscopy is also covered to treat: bleeding from lesions such as vascular anomalies, ulceration or tumors; a foreign body (removal); colonic polyps (excision); pseudo-obstruction of the colon (Ogilvie's syndrome, decompression); sigmoid volvulus or stricture; or narrowing or bleeding tumors, as palliative treatment (for example laser, electrocoagulation or stenting).
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-006, cov-027 to cov-031, cov-034.

criteria.text: Injections must be done under CT or fluoroscopic guidance with contrast. criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-013, cov-015, cov-017, cov-019 to cov-021.

criteria.text: Colonoscopy is generally not covered, unless the record documents why it is needed, for: chronic, stable irritable bowel syndrome or chronic abdominal pain (in unusual cases it may be done to rule out organic disease, especially when symptoms do not respond to therapy); acute diarrhea; hemorrhoids; routine follow-up of inflammatory bowel disease (cancer surveillance in Crohn's disease or chronic ulcerative colitis excepted); routine examination before elective abdominal surgery for a non-colonic disease; upper GI bleeding or black tarry stool with a demonstrated upper GI source; or bright red rectal bleeding with a convincing anorectal source on sigmoidoscopy and no other symptoms suggesting a source higher up. criteria.text: Active wound care (debridement) is covered to remove dead tissue and promote healing, performed with direct one-on-one patient contact, following accepted standards of wound treatment.

criteria.text: Patients identified as high risk for colon cancer are eligible for continued screening every 24 months.

Colonoscopy to investigate symptoms or findings is covered for: an imaging abnormality likely to be significant; unexplained bleeding (blood in the stool not thought to be from a rectal or perianal source, black tarry stool of unknown origin, or a positive stool blood test); unexplained iron-deficiency anemia; significant unexplained diarrhea with other findings such as weight loss; examining the whole colon for synchronous cancer or polyps in a patient with a treatable cancer or polyp; chronic inflammatory bowel disease when a more precise diagnosis or the extent of activity will change immediate management; locating during surgery a lesion that cannot be found by touch or sight; acute colonic ischemia; Streptococcus bovis endocarditis; unexplained new-onset constipation that does not respond to medical treatment; an anorectal adenomatous polyp; or infectious colitis.

criteria.text: Surveillance is covered for a history of colorectal cancer or polyps, follow-up one year after colorectal cancer surgery, follow-up after removal of a large sessile adenoma (more than 2 cm in its greatest dimension), and inflammatory bowel disease surveillance (pancolitis for more than 7 years, or left-sided colitis for more than 15 years; not for disease limited to the rectosigmoid).
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-013, cov-015, cov-017, cov-019 to cov-021.

criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-036 to cov-039, cov-041 to cov-049.

criteria.text: Colonoscopy is generally not covered, unless the record documents why it is needed, for: chronic, stable irritable bowel syndrome or chronic abdominal pain (in unusual cases it may be done to rule out organic disease, especially when symptoms do not respond to therapy); acute diarrhea; hemorrhoids; routine follow-up of inflammatory bowel disease (cancer surveillance in Crohn's disease or chronic ulcerative colitis excepted); routine examination before elective abdominal surgery for a non-colonic disease; upper GI bleeding or black tarry stool with a demonstrated upper GI source; or bright red rectal bleeding with a convincing anorectal source on sigmoidoscopy and no other symptoms suggesting a source higher up. criteria.text: Routine foot care is covered for nerve damage in the feet (without blood-vessel impairment) severe enough that care by a non-professional would put the patient at risk. The record must document loss of protective sensation: no feeling at 2 or more of 5 sites on either foot with the 5.07 Semmes-Weinstein monofilament.
It is covered for patients on blood thinners when the record documents the significant risk of non-professional foot care.

Foot care that would otherwise be routine is covered when a systemic condition, such as diabetes, arteriosclerosis obliterans, Buerger's disease, chronic thrombophlebitis or a peripheral neuropathy involving the feet, causes severe circulatory problems or areas of reduced sensation in the legs or feet, so that care by a non-professional would be hazardous. A diagnosis alone does not show the severity: the record must show it, for example by a non-traumatic amputation of the foot or part of it; two Class B findings (absent posterior tibial pulse, absent dorsalis pedis pulse, or advanced trophic changes, three of which are needed); or one Class B and two Class C findings (claudication, temperature changes such as cold feet, edema, paresthesias, burning). For diabetes, chronic thrombophlebitis and the neuropathies marked in the manual, the patient must be under the active care of a doctor of medicine or osteopathy who documents the condition.
criteria.source: Medicare Benefit Policy Manual Ch. 15 §290.C.3, §290.D, §290.F, §290.G; LCD L33941 v23 cov-000.

criteria.text: Active wound care (debridement) is covered to remove dead tissue and promote healing, performed with direct one-on-one patient contact, following accepted standards of wound treatment.

When the goal of care is not healing, the patient is managed under palliative care standards.

criteria.text: Patients identified as high risk for colon cancer are eligible for continued screening every 24 months.

Colonoscopy to investigate symptoms or findings is covered for: an imaging abnormality likely to be significant; unexplained bleeding (blood in the stool not thought to be from a rectal or perianal source, black tarry stool of unknown origin, or a positive stool blood test); unexplained iron-deficiency anemia; significant unexplained diarrhea with other findings such as weight loss; examining the whole colon for synchronous cancer or polyps in a patient with a treatable cancer or polyp; chronic inflammatory bowel disease when a more precise diagnosis or the extent of activity will change immediate management; locating during surgery a lesion that cannot be found by touch or sight; acute colonic ischemia; Streptococcus bovis endocarditis; unexplained new-onset constipation that does not respond to medical treatment; an anorectal adenomatous polyp; or infectious colitis.
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-007, cov-009 to cov-012, cov-014, cov-022 to cov-026, cov-032, cov-033, doc-001.

criteria.text: Surveillance is covered for a history of colorectal cancer or polyps, follow-up one year after colorectal cancer surgery, follow-up after removal of a large sessile adenoma (more than 2 cm in its greatest dimension), and inflammatory bowel disease surveillance (pancolitis for more than 7 years, or left-sided colitis for more than 15 years; not for disease limited to the rectosigmoid).
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-013, cov-015, cov-017, cov-019 to cov-021.

criteria.text: Colonoscopy is generally not covered, unless the record documents why it is needed, for: chronic, stable irritable bowel syndrome or chronic abdominal pain (in unusual cases it may be done to rule out organic disease, especially when symptoms do not respond to therapy); acute diarrhea; hemorrhoids; routine follow-up of inflammatory bowel disease (cancer surveillance in Crohn's disease or chronic ulcerative colitis excepted); routine examination before elective abdominal surgery for a non-colonic disease; upper GI bleeding or black tarry stool with a demonstrated upper GI source; or bright red rectal bleeding with a convincing anorectal source on sigmoidoscopy and no other symptoms suggesting a source higher up. It is also generally not covered for fulminant colitis, possible perforation, acute severe diverticulitis, or diverticulosis as the reason for the test (it may still be reported when it is the final diagnosis).
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-036 to cov-039, cov-041 to cov-049.

criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-006, cov-027 to cov-031, cov-034.

criteria.text: Patients identified as high risk for colon cancer are eligible for continued screening every 24 months.

Colonoscopy to investigate symptoms or findings is covered for: an imaging abnormality likely to be significant; unexplained bleeding (blood in the stool not thought to be from a rectal or perianal source, black tarry stool of unknown origin, or a positive stool blood test); unexplained iron-deficiency anemia; significant unexplained diarrhea with other findings such as weight loss; examining the whole colon for synchronous cancer or polyps in a patient with a treatable cancer or polyp; chronic inflammatory bowel disease when a more precise diagnosis or the extent of activity will change immediate management; locating during surgery a lesion that cannot be found by touch or sight; acute colonic ischemia; Streptococcus bovis endocarditis; unexplained new-onset constipation that does not respond to medical treatment; an anorectal adenomatous polyp; or infectious colitis.
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-007, cov-009 to cov-012, cov-014, cov-022 to cov-026, cov-032, cov-033, doc-001.

criteria.text: Surveillance is covered for a history of colorectal cancer or polyps, follow-up one year after colorectal cancer surgery, follow-up after removal of a large sessile adenoma (more than 2 cm in its greatest dimension), and inflammatory bowel disease surveillance (pancolitis for more than 7 years, or left-sided colitis for more than 15 years; not for disease limited to the rectosigmoid).
criteria.source: LCD L34005 v34 cov-013, cov-015, cov-017, cov-019 to cov-021.

criteria.text: Colonoscopy is generally not covered, unless the record documents why it is needed, for: chronic, stable irritable bowel syndrome or chronic abdominal pain (in unusual cases it may be done to rule out organic disease, especially when symptoms do not respond to therapy); acute diarrhea; hemorrhoids; routine follow-up of inflammatory bowel disease (cancer surveillance in Crohn's disease or chronic ulcerative colitis excepted); routine examination before elective abdominal surgery for a non-colonic disease; upper GI bleeding or black tarry stool with a demonstrated upper GI source; or bright red rectal bleeding with a convincing anorectal source on sigmoidoscopy and no other symptoms suggesting a source higher up. It is also generally not covered for fulminant colitis, possible perforation, acute severe diverticulitis, or diverticulosis as the reason for the test (it may still be reported when it is the final diagnosis).

criteria.text: Patch testing is covered to diagnose allergic contact dermatitis, or other dermatitis or skin eruptions where a contact allergen is the likely cause, when there is a clear-cut clinical suspicion of contact allergy and the chemicals tested are relevant to the problem.

criteria.text: Eyelid surgery is covered when it corrects visual impairment caused by excess eyelid skin weighing down the lashes (dermatochalasis), blepharochalasis, drooping of the eyelid (blepharoptosis) or drooping of the brow. It is also covered as reconstruction: to repair defects caused by disease (including thyroid disease and cranial nerve palsies), trauma or tumor surgery; for ectropion or entropion, epiblepharon, lagophthalmos, congenital ectropion, entropion, lagophthalmos or ptosis; for lid retraction or lag caused by horizontal laxity of the lower eyelid without ectropion or entropion (with exposure keratopathy or tearing), by horizontal laxity of the upper eyelid (with floppy eyelid syndrome), or by orbital thyroid disease; for chronic symptomatic dermatitis of the pretarsal skin caused by redundant upper eyelid skin; or, when other treatments have failed or cannot be used, to relieve blepharospasm. For these reconstructive conditions, the record must document the patient's complaints and the examination findings.
criteria.source: LCD L33944 v27 cov-016, cov-017, cov-019 to cov-022, cov-030 to cov-043.

criteria.text: For dermatochalasis, blepharochalasis, blepharoptosis or brow ptosis, the record must document the patient's complaints of functional problems, such as vision blocked above or to the side, trouble reading because the upper field is lost, or looking through the eyelashes or seeing eyelid skin. The reconstructive conditions are exempt.
criteria.source: LCD L33944 v27 cov-016, cov-024 to cov-027.

criteria.text: For dermatochalasis, blepharochalasis, blepharoptosis or brow ptosis, visual field testing must show a significant loss of upper vision (at least 12 degrees or 30 percent) that the surgery could correct. The reconstructive conditions are exempt.
For dermatochalasis, blepharochalasis, blepharoptosis or brow ptosis, eyelid surgery without documented functional impairment is considered cosmetic and is not covered.

criteria.text: A transthoracic echocardiogram is covered when the patient has symptoms of, or an existing condition in, one of these: weakened heart muscle or cardiomyopathy; hypertensive heart disease with clinical evidence of heart disease; heart attack or coronary insufficiency; exposure to drugs or treatments toxic to the heart; heart transplant or rejection monitoring; native heart valve disease; prosthetic heart valves; acute endocarditis; pericardial disease; aortic disease; congenital heart disease; suspected clots or embolic sources in the heart; heart tumors or masses; critical illness or trauma; arrhythmias or palpitations; fainting (syncope); or pulmonary heart disease, such as unexplained pulmonary hypertension or a pulmonary embolism with suspected clots in the right heart.
High blood pressure alone, without signs or symptoms of heart disease, is not a covered reason.

Repeating the study more often than once a year is generally not medically necessary unless the notes document a discrete episode of deterioration (an abrupt change in signs or symptoms), a check of the response to treatment, or imminent valve surgery.

criteria.text: Injections must be done under CT or fluoroscopic guidance with contrast. Without contrast, for example under ultrasound guidance, they are covered only when a contraindication to contrast, such as an allergy or pregnancy, is documented. A procedure code that includes imaging guidance counts as evidence of guidance, but contrast use, or the documented contraindication, must be in the notes. Interlaminar and caudal injections are limited to one level, and transforaminal injections to two levels in one spinal region.
criteria.source: LCD L33906 v75 cov-015, cov-016, cov-017, cov-020, cov-025; decision D-ESI-7.

criteria.text: A repeat injection is covered when the first one gave at least 50% improvement in pain lasting at least 3 months, or at least 50% improvement in function, on the same scale as the baseline. If the first injection did not work well, a repeat after at least 14 days is covered with a different approach, level or medication, when the reason for it is documented.
criteria.source: LCD L33906 v75 cov-019, cov-039; decision D-ESI-2.
